children: The Indian rupee's opening rally on Thursday faded slightly as banks with large importer client books stepped in to buy dollars, traders said, offsetting a part optimism sparked by parked by hefty inflows from one-off measures.
was at 94.46 per dollar at 1.04 pm IST, having rallied to a two-month high of 94.30 at open after the Reserve Bank of India's special measures drew far more inflows than expected.
The rupee not being able to add to its opening rally "was not unexpected", Kunal Kurani, vice president at Mecklai Finanical said.
A fall of more than a rupee in dollar/rupee over a short period was always likely to draw importer demand, he said.
Importers bought dollars after the rupee's opening rally, a private-sector bank trader said, with banks serving large importers among the buyers.
Oil remains a key concern for importers as crude prices rise after renewed U.S. strikes on Iran, bankers and analysts said.
A sustained rise in oil prices would widen India's import bill and put pressure on the trade deficit, making importers more inclined to lock in their dollar requirements.
The renewed rally in crude are fanning inflation concerns, pushing bond yields higher and making markets more wary that Federal Reserve may need to raise rates this month.
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield has climbed its highest level in nearly three years, while bets on a September Fed rate hike have climbed to 2-in-3.
